clue.text: In the main I spout about church a great deal

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
a great deal means a lot

explanation.surface: A preacher admits to going on about the church at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' sounds like 'mostly' but means 'in the sea': the whale speaks of itself spouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sperm whale lives in the ocean and blows a spout of vapour, so it can describe itself this way.

clue.text: Said clergyman needs support when under attack

indicators.note: said tells us the words are spoken, so we hear their sound rather than their spelling

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman and aid is support; spoken together they make the sound we need

explanation.surface: A priest who is being attacked needs backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannonade is a sustained bombardment by artillery, an attack with heavy guns.

clue.text: Pass round a place for snakes in Roman temple

indicators.note: round says the mountain pass goes about the other pieces

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a snake pit is a place where snakes are kept

explanation.surface: Walking past a snake pit on the way to an ancient Roman shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a verb in the surface but is a mountain col.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capitol was the temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill in ancient Rome.

clue.text: A stock of words used by man or Eric woman

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'A stock of words used by man or Eric woman': A + LEXIS fits, but 'Eric' sits inside the definition 'man or woman' and does no job; likely an OCR intrusion, and the scan is blank.

clue.text: Building old and, as you see, incomplete

parts.note: thou is the old form of you

indicators.note: incomplete says the word see loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened

explanation.surface: A building described as ancient and, as you can see, unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as you see' is updated to the archaic 'as thou see', with 'incomplete' cutting the last E of SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast house is a kiln building used for drying hops, typical of Kent in southern England.

clue.text: State one's in after very good party

indicators.note: after places the state with its insertion behind the word for very

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: in says the letter for one goes inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A State Department official joins a very good party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good' adds nothing to the wordplay; it only colours the surface. Cal is the old postal abbreviation for California.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or gathering, such as a church social.

clue.text: Music mostly has secured employment for one of the Beatles?

indicators.note: has secured says the shortened music holds the employment inside it
mostly says the last letter is removed

parts.note: a score is written music
use means employment, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: Music largely gets one of the Beatles a job.
explanation.walkthrough: SCORE less its last letter is SCOR, which holds USE: SCO-USE-R.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scouser is a native of Liverpool, as all the Beatles were, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Inquisitive types behave so strangely

definitions.meaning: nosy people act in a prying, questioning manner

explanation.surface: Nosy people act oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Curiously means both in an inquisitive manner and oddly or strangely.

clue.text: Paint thinner's brilliant colour

parts.note: ace means brilliant or excellent
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A paint thinner gives a brilliant colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a solvent used to thin paint and remove nail varnish.

clue.text: Son abandons children's card game for one akin to whist

indicators.note: abandons says the letter for son is dropped from the card game

parts.note: snap is a simple card game played by children

explanation.surface: A boy gives up a nursery card game for a grown-up game like whist.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap, short for Napoleon, is a trick-taking card game similar to whist.

clue.text: A tour's been organised somewhere on the south coast

indicators.note: organised says the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A trip has been arranged to a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastbourne is a seaside town in East Sussex on the south coast of England.

clue.text: Altogether a successful 1997 election slogan?

definitions.meaning: in 1997 Labour swept the Conservatives from power, so a call to throw the right wing out won

explanation.surface: A one-word answer that is also a winning party catchphrase from Labour's 1997 landslide.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it says 'out, right!', the voters' verdict on the Conservatives in the 1997 UK general election.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means wholly or completely, a synonym for altogether.

clue.text: Exactly what soiled garment had?

definitions.meaning: precisely right, as in a correct guess
a dirty garment has a mark or stain on it

explanation.surface: Precisely describing what a stained shirt has.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is a British idiom meaning exactly right or precisely correct.

clue.text: Showers in some parts of London causing troubles

indicators.note: Cockney speech in parts of London drops the initial h sound

parts.note: hails, as a verb, means showers down, as hail does

explanation.surface: Rainfall in some London districts causes problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link; 'Showers' is a verb here, and Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop their Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ails means troubles or afflicts, as in 'what ails you?'.

clue.text: Pile of rubbish resulting from unwieldy paper chase that's endless

indicators.note: unwieldy describes something clumsy and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
endless says the last letter of chase is removed

parts.note: taken as written before it loses its end

explanation.surface: An awkward cross-country paper chase ends up as a heap of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's endless' trims CHASE to CHAS; PAPER plus CHAS is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a pile of discarded waste material and junk.

clue.text: Cancelled drink with leading journalist?

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a press editor, abbreviated press ed, is a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A news item killed after drinks with a senior reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: One who sups with the press editor may well get a story buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppressed means stopped from being published or put down, so cancelled.

clue.text: Gently touch part of body, taking temperature in medical procedure

parts.note: to pat is to touch gently

indicators.note: taking says the chest takes the letter for temperature inside it

parts.note: the chest is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A doctor gently pats your chest while taking your temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: A patch test, used to check for skin allergies, needs no thermometer: 'taking temperature' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch test is a skin test for allergies, applying substances under a patch.

clue.text: Application for the stage

definitions.meaning: a stagecoach, especially a French public coach of old

explanation.surface: A request to work in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence is careful steady effort, and a diligence was also a public stagecoach in France.

clue.text: Even tart is unrecognisable, appearing in drag

indicators.note: unrecognisable says the letters are scrambled beyond recognition

explanation.surface: Even a tart can't be recognised when she turns up dressed as a man.
explanation.definitionFit: En travesti is a French theatre phrase for playing a role dressed as the opposite sex.

clue.text: Failure of one dramatic work, then another shortly

parts.note: Noh is a form of classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: shortly says the word for that work is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an opera is another dramatic work

explanation.surface: A play flops, and then a second one, briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is a person or thing with no chance of success, a failure.

clue.text: Subject: problem in the bloody tube

indicators.note: in says the problem goes inside the tube

parts.note: a vein is a tube carrying blood
ill as a noun means a problem or misfortune

explanation.surface: A medical issue in a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A villein was a feudal serf, a subject of the lord of the manor.

clue.text: Always carried back in boat? The reverse

indicators.note: back says those held letters are read in reverse
carried says the boat is held inside the word always

explanation.surface: A clue that playfully reverses itself: something always carried in a boat, or rather the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' and 'in' are links: the surface says always is carried in a boat, but it is the boat that is carried, backwards, inside 'Always' (LWAY).
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing boat with a small mizzen mast aft.

clue.text: Permanent struggle involving India Call 0870 and GB

clue.text: Up at six in Spain after this?

definitions.text: Up at six in Spain after this?

parts.words: Up at six in Spain after this?
parts.note: in Spain people rest in the heat of the afternoon and are up again at about six in the evening

explanation.surface: A Spaniard rising at six in the evening after a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up at six' suggests rising early in the morning; it is six in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap traditional in Spain, after which people rise.

clue.text: Place of worship for union members

definitions.meaning: a small church or a room for prayer
a branch of a printers' or journalists' trade union

explanation.surface: A church used by trade unionists.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a place of Christian worship and also a branch of a printing trade union.

clue.text: Presiding over discussion companion initiates

indicators.note: initiates says the companion starts off the word for discussion

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour
an airing is a public discussion of a view

explanation.surface: Running a debate opened by a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairing means presiding over a meeting as its chair.

clue.text: Such as DJs having urge to introduce record

indicators.note: to introduce says the urge takes the record inside it

parts.note: to press is to urge
to enter is to record, as in a log

explanation.surface: Radio DJs wanting to play a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link; 'record' is a verb here, as in entering details in a log.
explanation.definitionFit: DJs are examples of presenters, people who host broadcast programmes.

clue.text: Popular name for pub

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A well-known name for a public house.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub, especially one offering lodging.

clue.text: Surgery held by doctor before home visit

indicators.note: held by says the surgery is attached to the doctor, following it

parts.note: OP is short for operation, surgery
in means at home

explanation.surface: A doctor holds an operation before a house call.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-in is a casual unannounced visit.

clue.text: Finish off rum, imbibing litre

indicators.note: imbibing says the word for rum drinks in the letter for litre

parts.note: rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: Polishing off rum while downing a litre.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle is to kill by choking, to finish someone off.
